title: Improving Social Network Embedding via New Second-Order Continuous Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: Existing graph neural networks may be unsuitable for real-world web applications because over-smoothing can affect personalized recommendations and limited prediction explanation can hinder understanding in business scenarios.

gap.claim: Prevailing first-order continuous GNN frameworks require heuristic feature augmentation for numerical stability, intrinsically exhibit over-smoothing through diffusion, and face difficulties integrating graph topology into ODEs.

contributions.claim: A second-order continuous graph neural network framework is proposed to address limitations of first-order continuous GNNs.
A semi-model-agnostic method based on the proposed model is introduced to enhance prediction explanation using high-order information.
An analogy between continuous GNNs and selected partial differential equations is constructed, with properties of first- and second-order models discussed.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method and that it outperforms related baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs are powerful tools for web research problems, but existing models are not fully suitable for many real-world applications.
Over-smoothing and limited prediction explanation create application challenges, while first-order continuous GNNs have stability, smoothing, and topology-integration limitations.
The paper proposes a second-order continuous GNN, views it as a coupled first-order model, and adds a high-order-information explanation method.
The authors relate continuous GNNs to partial differential equations and discuss properties of first- and second-order models.
The authors report that extensive experiments outperform related baselines.
